text: Nine lessons ago, this project started with one sentence from Priya Suresh: migrate the catalog app to Azure before launch, the images and the server itself. Here's everything that sentence turned into.

A scope statement, then a plan split into two real pieces. Real Azure resources: a tagged resource group, a storage account, a virtual machine. The product images, moved into Blob Storage at the Hot tier. The application, standing on vm-catalog01, serving real traffic. Monitoring the on-prem server never had: a Log Analytics workspace and a real CPU alert. All of it tested end to end, documented in a runbook, and presented to Priya as a concrete cutover plan.

None of these lessons were really about the Azure CLI alone. Requirements clarification. Scoping down to match the actual ask. Provisioning deliberately, not by habit. Validating by testing, not by assuming. Communicating clearly to a stakeholder and a team. The CLI commands were the vehicle -- these are what actually made the project succeed.

This project was scoped smaller than Driftwood's full cloud picture on purpose: one app, one VM, no auto-scaling, no containers, no automated pipeline, one stakeholder. That wasn't a limitation to apologize for -- it was the correct scope for the actual request.

One migrated application doesn't mean Driftwood's cloud journey is finished. The business reasons behind this migration -- growing traffic, less tolerance for downtime, a team depending on these systems daily -- don't stop applying just because this one project is done. Driftwood's platform needs will keep growing well beyond what one app on one VM can carry.

Exactly what that growth looks like, and how to meet it, is its own project -- not something to guess at here. This Beginner capstone is complete: one real workload, migrated, monitored, documented, and handed off the right way.
